thread:
Thomas Baird: Heads up: as we roll out burn-rate alerts for tiered SLOs, we need to update alert routing + oncall schedules this week. Current Alertmanager routes basically dump everything into platform-oncall, which will be noisy once Hosted/Dedicated get split.

Rafael Mendes: +1. SRE needs Dedicated burn alerts to page dedicated-oncall (different escalation) and Hosted to page platform-oncall. Can we get this into the next change window?

Sergio Costa: From the dashboards/alerts PR, the new rules all have labels:
- `tier=hosted|dedicated`
- `slo=<name>` (api_availability, embeddings_latency, pool_readiness, etc)
- `service=<gateway|routing|scheduler|control-plane>`
We just need routing on `tier` + `severity`.

Allison Grant: Also reminder: burn alerts are multi-window, so you’ll see pairs (fast burn / slow burn) for the same SLO. We should group by `tier,slo,region` so PD doesn’t explode.

Connor O'Brien: For change mgmt: if this impacts paging destinations, we need an approval + a comms ping to #eng-oncall. Please include rollback steps.

Thomas Baird: Proposed Alertmanager routes (staging first):
```yaml
route:
  receiver: "platform-oncall"
  group_by: ["alertname", "tier", "slo", "region"]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 2h
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - tier="dedicated"
        - severity=~"page|critical"
      receiver: "dedicated-oncall"
    - matchers:
        - tier="hosted"
        - severity=~"page|critical"
      receiver: "platform-oncall"
    - matchers:
        - severity="ticket"
      receiver: "sre-triage"
```
Then receivers map to PD services.

PagerDuty Bot: Thomas Baird invited you to connect Alertmanager → PagerDuty integration: "redwood-prod-am". Use /pd link to authorize.

Peter Holtz: One gotcha: "protective throttling" alerts (Hosted) should page platform-oncall but NOT wake up Dedicated folks even if the underlying routing service is shared. Labeling has to be tier-first.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Also Dedicated "pool_readiness" we said ticket-only for dips <5m, page only if sustained + customer-impact likely. Do we have that encoded as `severity` in the rule?

Sergio Costa: Yep, current rule template:
- `DedicatedPoolReadinessLow` -> severity=ticket
- `DedicatedPoolReadinessLowSustained` (30m) -> severity=page
Both label tier=dedicated.

Thomas Baird: Cool. Next: PagerDuty services/schedules. Right now we have:
- "Platform Oncall" (schedule: platform-primary/platform-secondary)
- "Dedicated Oncall" exists but isn’t wired to alertmanager yet (only some manual escalations).
We should create a dedicated service just for SLO burn pages? Or reuse existing dedicated service?

Rafael Mendes: Reuse existing Dedicated Oncall service if possible. We want a single place to see incidents, regardless of source (capacity, customer escalation, SLO burn). But we do want different urgency mapping (burn = high unless severity=ticket).

Allison Grant: +1 on reusing. For ticket severity, can route to Jira instead of PD. But if you keep it in PD, set it as low urgency + no phone.

Connor O'Brien: If we create new PD services, please document ownership and escalation policy. We had issues with orphan services last quarter.

Thomas Baird: Plan:
1) Add `tier`-based routing in Alertmanager (staging today, prod tomorrow).
2) Map receivers:
   - platform-oncall -> PD Service: Platform Oncall
   - dedicated-oncall -> PD Service: Dedicated Oncall
   - sre-triage -> Jira (ENG-SRE queue) + Slack #eng-sre
3) Update PD escalation policies so "ticket" doesn’t page. (We can set `severity=ticket` to go via webhook to Jira, bypass PD.)

Peter Holtz: Can we make sure alerts include runbook link? If it lands in #eng-sre but not in PD, folks still need the runbook.

Sergio Costa: In the rule annotations we include:
- `runbook_url`
- `dashboard_url`
- `slo_spec_url`
Those should pass through to PD + Jira.

Thomas Baird: Re oncall schedule names: do we have an official schedule ID for Dedicated? I see "dedicated-primary" but it’s empty next week.

INTake Bot: Linked ticket created: INT-1188 "Update alert routing/oncall rotations for burn-rate SLO alerts" (assignee: Thomas Baird). Priority: High.

Rafael Mendes: That empty schedule is real (lol). Dedicated team hasn’t updated rotations for Feb. I’ll ping Vanessa + Gabe to fix today. We can’t flip routing if it pages nobody.

Thomas Baird: Thanks. I’ll keep the prod change behind a feature flag on the alertmanager config until the schedule is populated.

Connor O'Brien: Please post in #eng-oncall once staging is validated. Also add a rollback note: revert alertmanager config + restart.

Thomas Baird: Will do. Staging deploy at 3pm PT. If no regressions by EOD, prod at 10am PT tomorrow. I’ll drop a checklist in INT-1188.

PagerDuty Bot: Change logged: "Dedicated Oncall" escalation policy edited by Thomas Baird. (Pending approval)

Thomas Baird: (for approval context) change is adding a second target (dedicated-secondary) and setting burn alerts to "High urgency" only when severity=page. Ticket path goes to Jira, not PD.

Allison Grant: Sounds right. Once live, can we sample a few alerts to confirm group_by works? We shouldn’t get 20 pages per region/model.

Thomas Baird: Yep. I’ll force-fire one Hosted burn + one Dedicated burn in staging and confirm grouping + routing. Will post screenshots + PD incident links in INT-1188.
